- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model often overcorrects; cap forecast at +2% above true peak.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); apply +1.5–2.5% bias to first 5 days.
- When sentiment history shows alternating +/– signals, model exhibits mean reversion bias; adjust forecast to align with recent 3–5 day average if sentiment is neutral.
- If sentiment is consistently positive over 3+ days, model tends to overpredict; apply downward correction proportional to sentiment strength (e.g., 0.5x sentiment value as offset).
